<description>
While reviewing #36642 I found something else we missed in JSON-RPC 2.0:

If we receive a malformed request we would assume that we couldn't parse it's jsonrpc version and send an HTTP error.  This is how the legacy jsonrpc server worked (despite that behavior not ever being part of any ratified jsonrpc spec) and we maintain it as Bitcoin "legacy" jsonrpc protocol. However it's possible to form a request that does properly indicate jsonrpc 2.0 but is still malformed. In that case, we should not send an HTTP error: the correct protocol is to respond with `HTTP 200 OK` and include the jsonrpc error message in the response.

The solution is to check if we know the request's jsonrpc version before responding with an error.

We already correctly handle such malformed requests in batches and this is already tested in `test_batch_requests()` in `interface_rpc.py`

On master, the functional test in this PR actually crashes the node because the assumption is codified. Note that this crash requires:
1. RPC Authentication
2. A debug build

So this is not an urgent security fix, but a bug that might disrupt testing.

```
node0 stderr httprpc.cpp:46
    UniValue JSONErrorReply(UniValue, const JSONRPCRequest &, HTTPStatusCode &):
        'jreq.m_json_version != JSONRPCVersion::V2' check failed.
```

In release builds the node doesn't crash, but it returns HTTP 400 with a JSON-RPC 2.0 error body instead of HTTP 200.
</description>

9b21a79587 rpc: handle malformed jsonrpc 2.0 requests correctly

<patch>
diff --git a/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md b/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md
index a9ea089d4b..caa4376be0 100644
--- a/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md
+++ b/doc/JSON-RPC-interface.md
@@ -89,7 +89,7 @@ protocol in v27.0 and prior releases.
 | Request marker | `"version": "1.1"` (or none) | `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` |
 | Response marker | (none) | `"jsonrpc": "2.0"` |
 | `"error"` and `"result"` fields in response | both present | only one is present |
-| HTTP codes in response | `200` unless there is any kind of RPC error (invalid parameters, method not found, etc) | Always `200` unless there is an actual HTTP server error (request parsing error, endpoint not found, etc) |
+| HTTP codes in response | `200` unless there is any kind of RPC error (invalid parameters, method not found, etc) | Always `200` unless there is an actual HTTP server error (request body is not valid JSON, endpoint not found, etc) |
 | Notifications: requests that get no reply | (not supported) | Supported for requests that exclude the "id" field. Returns HTTP status `204` "No Content" |
 
 ## Security
diff --git a/src/rpc/request.cpp b/src/rpc/request.cpp
index f348ed983e..3a789a0585 100644
--- a/src/rpc/request.cpp
+++ b/src/rpc/request.cpp
@@ -68,7 +68,13 @@ UniValue JSONRPCReplyObj(UniValue result, UniValue error, std::optional<UniValue
         if (jsonrpc_version == JSONRPCVersion::V1_LEGACY) reply.pushKV("result", NullUniValue);
         reply.pushKV("error", std::move(error));
     }
-    if (id.has_value()) reply.pushKV("id", std::move(id.value()));
+    if (id.has_value()) {
+        reply.pushKV("id", std::move(id.value()));
+    } else if (jsonrpc_version == JSONRPCVersion::V2) {
+        // id is required in JSONRPC 2.0 responses, can be null if there
+        // was an error parsing the request.
+        reply.pushKV("id", NullUniValue);
+    }
     return reply;
 }
 
diff --git a/src/httprpc.cpp b/src/httprpc.cpp
index 0981de5f97..444b813ed9 100644
--- a/src/httprpc.cpp
+++ b/src/httprpc.cpp
@@ -40,10 +40,12 @@ static bool g_rpc_whitelist_default = false;
 
 static UniValue JSONErrorReply(UniValue objError, const JSONRPCRequest& jreq, HTTPStatusCode& nStatus)
 {
-    // HTTP errors should never be returned if JSON-RPC v2 was requested. This
-    // function should only be called when a v1 request fails or when a request
-    // cannot be parsed, so the version is unknown.
-    Assume(jreq.m_json_version != JSONRPCVersion::V2);
+    // A request known to be JSON-RPC 2.0 gets the error in the reply with HTTP OK
+    // HTTP error statuses are only returned for 1.x requests and requests whose version is unknown.
+    if (jreq.m_json_version == JSONRPCVersion::V2) {
+        nStatus = HTTP_OK;
+        return JSONRPCReplyObj(NullUniValue, std::move(objError), jreq.id, jreq.m_json_version);
+    }
 
     // Send error reply from json-rpc error object
     nStatus = HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;
diff --git a/test/functional/interface_rpc.py b/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
index d9636c122a..c7c76492d0 100755
--- a/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
+++ b/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
@@ -225,6 +225,35 @@ class RPCInterfaceTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         # Sanity check: command was not executed
         assert_equal(block_count + 1, self.nodes[0].getblockcount())
 
+        self.log.info("Testing error handling of requests with malformed body")
+        cases = [
+            ({},                                       "Missing method"),
+            ({"method": 1},                            "Method must be a string"),
+            ({"method": "getblockcount", "params": 1}, "Params must be an array or object"),
+        ]
+        self.log.info("... JSONRPC 1.1 expects HTTP error codes")
+        for request, message in cases:
+            response, status = send_json_rpc(self.nodes[0], {**request})
+            assert_equal(
+                response,
+                {'result': None, 'error': {'code': -32600, 'message': message}}
+            )
+            assert_equal(status, 400)
+        self.log.info("... JSONRPC 2.0 expects HTTP 200 with error message in response")
+        for request, message in cases:
+            for notification in [True, False]:
+                body = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", **request}
+                if not notification:
+                    body["id"] = "1"
+                response, status = send_json_rpc(self.nodes[0], body)
+                expected = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "error": {"code": RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, "message": message}}
+                if notification:
+                    expected["id"] = None
+                else:
+                    expected["id"] = "1"
+                assert_equal(response, expected)
+                assert_equal(status, 200)
+
     def test_work_queue_exceeded(self):
         self.log.info("Testing work queue exceeded...")
         self.restart_node(0, ['-rpcworkqueue=1', '-rpcthreads=1'])

</patch>
